name: Dhabriya Polywood Ltd
tagline: Jaipur maker + installer of uPVC/PVC profiles, windows and modular furniture (brand 'Polywood'), now scaling a genuine second growth leg (aluminium windows/facade, Rs56cr+ backlog) with PAT compounding far faster than revenue (+67% FY26, +35% Q1 FY27 on ~10-12% topline growth) -- a clean, cheap (~16x) small-cap compounder, but still no 10x path at this scale
business_overview: Dhabriya Polywood extrudes uPVC/PVC profiles under the 'Polywood' brand and makes uPVC windows and doors, modular furniture, and (newer, higher-margin) fluted and soffit wall panels; a new Aluminium Windows & Facade division is scaling with a Rs56cr+ order backlog guided to contribute Rs40-50cr revenue in FY27. It sells directly to builders -- including luxury developers DLF, M3M, Emaar and Godrej Properties -- and offers end-to-end solutions including installation, which lifts its margin profile versus panel-only peers. FY25 segment revenue: PVC profiles ~Rs 135 Cr, uPVC windows ~Rs 60 Cr, modular furniture ~Rs 40 Cr, with fluted/soffit panels ~Rs 40 Cr inside the profile segment. Extrusion capacity ~24,000 MTPA; windows ~13 lakh sq ft. A Board-approved Rs100 Cr capex programme (FY26-FY28) is funding a Jaipur facility upgrade and the facade capacity build-out.
fundamentals_table: FY22 Rs134Cr/Rs5Cr, FY23 Rs171Cr/Rs8Cr, FY24 Rs211Cr/Rs14Cr, FY25 Rs235Cr/Rs18Cr, FY26 Rs264Cr/Rs30Cr -- PAT +67% FY26 on only +12.6% revenue growth
Revenue Rs 68.31 Cr (+10.0% YoY); PAT Rs 8.86 Cr (+35.4% YoY); EBITDA Rs15.76Cr (+27.6%); EBITDA margin 23.07% vs 19.90% YoY (+317bps)

Order book Rs 200 Cr+ (all-time high); Aluminium Windows & Facade division backlog Rs56Cr+ guided to deliver Rs40-50Cr FY27 revenue; Rs 100 Cr capex (FY26-FY28: ~Rs27Cr deployed FY26, Rs35-40Cr guided FY27 for Jaipur upgrade, Rs20-30Cr FY28)

Borrowings rose to Rs76Cr (Mar-2026) from Rs53Cr (Mar-2025) as the capex programme ramps -- a reversal of the earlier multi-year deleveraging trend, not yet a concern given rising ROCE but a genuine change from the prior 'debt reduced, advances nil' picture
~15.5-17x trailing (recent quotes conflict: Rs465-520 price range, Sept 2026)
Rs0.70/share recommended with FY26 results (May-2026 board meeting) -- dividend initiated

Promoter (Digvijay Dhabriya) ~67.75-67.8%, stable for the last ~4 quarters (Sep2025-Jun2026) after declining from 74.22% (Mar2023); Ashish Kacholia held ~5.3% as of Jun-2026 (one dated source claims a full exit via Surya Vanshi Pvt Ltd with Abakkus Fund/Sunil Singhania stepping in -- not corroborated by the more recent Jun-2026 shareholding disclosure, treat as unresolved); Mukul Agarwal's current position not independently re-confirmed this pass
fundamentals_narrative: A genuinely good, improving small-cap: ROCE stepped up from ~19% (FY24) to ~26% (FY26), and PAT is now compounding far faster than revenue (+67% FY26, +35.4% Q1 FY27) on margin expansion (EBITDA margin +317bps YoY in Q1 FY27) as the mix shifts toward higher-margin fluted/soffit panels, end-to-end installation, and the new Aluminium Windows & Facade division. Revenue growth itself has stayed muted (~10-12% in FY25-FY26 and Q1 FY27, down from ~23-28% in FY22-FY24) -- but this reflects an extended monsoon plus Delhi-NCR GRAP construction restrictions (FY25) and deferred site execution by large developers in Maharashtra/Delhi NCR (FY26), not weakening demand: the order book (Rs200Cr+, including a new Rs56Cr+ facade backlog) is at an all-time high, well ahead of the reported run-rate. The company is funding a Rs100Cr multi-year capex programme partly through rising debt (borrowings Rs53Cr->Rs76Cr in the last year) -- a reversal of the earlier deleveraging narrative, though returns are still rising alongside it. A maiden dividend (Rs0.70/share) was recommended with FY26 results. The constraint on the thesis remains scale: at ~Rs68Cr quarterly revenue, the honest multi-year return is ~2-3x, not 10x, even if order-book conversion normalizes and margin keeps expanding.
technical_read: Not pulled. Stock had corrected ~35% from its all-time high as of the 2024 thread discussion; has since re-rated with the margin improvement, though recent quoted prices (Rs465-520) vary across sources.
sentiment_summary: Thread of ~64 posts spanning 2018-2026. Early history carried a governance flag: dineshssairam (trusted, elevated) took then exited a tracking position in 2020, citing 'too many related-party transactions, especially on the balance sheet (debt)'. That concern was subsequently, at least partly, mitigated -- dhruvrawani (2022) and others noted borrowings were reduced and loans & advances taken to nil (a trend that has now partly reversed as the FY26-28 capex programme is funded with fresh borrowings, per this pass's research). The 2024-2026 tone is constructive: Mayank_Jham on the DLF/M3M/Emaar order pipeline and the fluted-panel trend; Nitya_Shah (9 love) reporting an analyst's plant visit that 'preferred Dhabriya over Kaka Industries' for its end-to-end model and higher margins; aditya.lathe's detailed Sept-2025 plant-visit notes on the higher-margin soffit-panel demand, resin-price tailwind, and the BIS-certification / potential anti-dumping-duty-on-profiles optionality; yash_bhalani (invested) on the new facade-solutions segment, which this pass confirms has since won its first named orders (Godrej Properties, Rs4.78Cr external facade; other aluminium-doors/windows orders of Rs10.63Cr and Rs15.17Cr).
community_signal: Mildly positive from non-trusted-but-thorough trackers (plant visits, order-book detail). The one elevated-tier voice on record, dineshssairam, was negative in 2020 on RPTs -- a view that predates the debt reduction and has not been restated since, though the recent re-leveraging (to fund capex) is worth watching against that original concern. No current trusted high-conviction call either way.

Structural drivers intact: uPVC-window penetration vs wood/aluminium, the fluted/soffit wall-panel decor trend, real-estate completions, and import substitution (BIS certification, ADD on resin, hoped-for ADD on finished profiles)

Cheap at ~15.5-17x trailing for a ~26% ROCE/ROE, margin-expanding business that just initiated its first dividend (Rs0.70/share) -- the reverse-P/E math suggests the market is pricing in only modest growth versus the demonstrated PAT trajectory

Score 2.5; valuation-box exception is technically available but deliberately not invoked (see verdict_reasoning) -- thesis_fit stays 'neither'.

Offsetting this: borrowings rose Rs53Cr->Rs76Cr in the last year to fund the new capex cycle (a real change from the prior deleveraging narrative), and Ashish Kacholia's current stake is unresolved between conflicting sources.

track_record.note: FY19-FY26 screener consolidated. Both revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% in the same FY: FY24 (+23%, ROCE 19%), FY25 (+11%, ROCE 20%), FY26 (+12.6%, ROCE 26%). The strong-growth years FY22 (+26%) and FY23 (+28%) had sub-15% ROCE; ROCE only stepped above 15% from FY24 as the mix shifted to higher-margin fluted/soffit panels + end-to-end installation, now reinforced by the facade division.

quality_metrics.note: FY26 ROCE ~25.6-26% / ROE ~26.3%, OPM expanded 10%->21% FY22->FY26 on mix, and Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was +317bps YoY (23.07% vs 19.90%). Borrowings rose to Rs76Cr (Mar-2026) from Rs53Cr (Mar-2025) to fund the new Rs100Cr capex programme -- net_debt_to_ebitda ticked up to ~1.4 from the prior ~1.3, still manageable given rising ROCE. deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Medium (no change, materially firmer evidence). ROCE rising to ~26%, PAT compounding at 35-67% YoY on genuine margin expansion, a second growth leg (Aluminium Windows & Facade) now with named orders won, and a maiden dividend initiated are real positives that firm up the existing Medium conviction rather than raising it further. Offsetting factors -- borrowings rising Rs53Cr->Rs76Cr to fund the new capex cycle (a reversal of the earlier deleveraging story), an unresolved discrepancy over Ashish Kacholia's current stake, and the still-sub-scale ~Rs68Cr quarterly revenue -- keep this a real quality small-cap rather than a re-rating candidate. four_box score unchanged at 2.5 (valuation yes, others weak); thesis_fit stays 'neither' as the return-magnitude exception, while technically available, continues not to be invoked given the honest ~2-3x multi-year return math.
